object_description: a compact square solitaire beneath an expressive curved shed roof
design_condition: The building is placed toward the north-east to create a generous public open space along the river and a welcoming school space toward the south, while strengthening slow-traffic connections.

positive.statement: The compact solitaire establishes dialogue with the adjacent large buildings and creates a spacious contiguous open space.
The river area is enhanced as an ecologically valuable compensation and local recreation space.
The public ground floor connects the building strongly with its attractive surroundings.
The learning landscape meaningfully combines classrooms, semi-classrooms, work areas, access areas, and courtyards.
The classrooms along the facade can be optimally illuminated and ventilated.
The gym is optimally illuminated through its raised position above the terrain.
The concentration in one building allows great freedom in designing the surrounding spaces and provides high public added value.
The learning-landscape concept promises diverse forms of teaching.

negative.statement: The all-weather pitch is somewhat too small.
Entry and exit from the main road, particularly for above-ground parking, are unresolved because the turning radius is too small.
The proposed room height is significantly too low for the entrance and multifunctional uses.
Mutual views across the courtyards into classrooms are negative.
The two basement levels and complex roof and facade construction prevent optimal economic efficiency.
The basement, roof, and facade construction have a detrimental effect on energy and sustainability.
The proposed southward expansion would leave the entrance, auditorium, and gallery areas poorly exposed and unattractive.
The expressive roof allows insufficiently specific engagement with the existing character and neighboring buildings.
The design is unfortunately somewhat too self-referential, especially in its treatment of neighboring buildings.
